size.note: Newman's Birds gives 20 cm. Wikipedia gives about 18 cm.

habitat: Clear, fast-flowing streams and rivers with well-wooded banks, often near rapids; also small, heavily wooded inland waters. Perches low over water on exposed roots or overhanging branches.
summary: A small river kingfisher, scarce in Kruger at the edge of its escarpment-stream range, and present in every month. Adults have a black bill, bright blue upperparts, a blue half-collar on each side of the breast, and cinnamon underparts. It is easily confused with the much commoner Malachite Kingfisher, which has a red bill as an adult and orange cheeks. Wikipedia is the only source used here for some red at the base of the female's lower mandible; Newman's and eBird do not state it. Juvenile and chick plumage are not described in the sources used here.

similar.note: Malachite is smaller (14 cm vs 20 cm), adults have a red bill and red-orange cheeks, and the turquoise crown reaches the eye. Juvenile Malachite also has a dark bill, but keeps orange on the face; Half-collared has a blue face with no orange (eBird; Newman's).
Pygmy has a red bill, mauve/violet ear-coverts and an orange eyebrow, is a summer visitor, and usually hunts in woodland away from water (Newman's).

bill.shape: long and dagger-shaped, with some red at the base of the lower mandible (Wikipedia only; Newman's and eBird do not state it)

viewNotes.note: Front-on, the cinnamon belly and the dark blue half-collar on each breast side frame a whitish throat. The face is blue, with no orange (eBird).
From behind, the upperparts are all bright blue, back to the rump (Newman's).
In side view, the long black bill and the red legs are the key marks against Malachite (Newman's).
Flies low and fast along the stream.
In flight the upperparts are bright blue, and the bird flies low and fast along the stream (Newman's). The underwing is not described in the sources used here.
